issues: The body uses bright lime green instead of the described Mega Man-style blue, changing the enemy's identity.
The middle black band is disproportionately heavy and visually splits the drone into two disconnected caps.
Both eyes are boxy white blocks with tiny square pupils rather than two clearly round mechanical eyes.
The top and bottom white-and-green stripes are rigid and symmetrical, giving the body a tiled pattern instead of convincing barrel curvature.
The stepped black corners and small bottom protrusions make the silhouette slightly lumpy at 1x.
The design is readable and palette-efficient, but lacks the distinctive asymmetry or expressive detail typical of a shippable MM2/MM3 enemy.
fixes: Replace the lime pixels with one medium NES blue; optionally use a lighter blue only for a compact highlight cluster.
Reduce the black eye band by one pixel vertically where possible and let the blue-white shell frame it more clearly.
Round each eye by cutting the four corner pixels from its white cluster, then place compact dark pupils consistently toward the travel direction.
Rework the upper and lower shell into broader curved white clusters with blue confined to side shading or a central panel, rather than alternating stripes.
Clean the lower silhouette by removing the isolated-looking black feet/protrusions and using a continuous stepped barrel curve.
Add one small Capcom-style character cue, such as offset pupils or a tiny underside thruster, without introducing extra colors or noise.

issues: The bright lime-green top and bottom panels do not match the specified white-and-blue body.
The silhouette has nearly straight sides and broad flat caps, reading more like a striped box than a barrel-shaped drone.
The central black band is excessively heavy and visually divides the sprite into three disconnected slabs.
Both eyes are square white blocks; their pupils merge into the surrounding black band, weakening the intended big round-eye character.
Perfectly repeated vertical stripes and rigid symmetry make the design feel like a modern pixel icon rather than an MM2/MM3 enemy.
The lower corner black clusters are bulky and make the outline look thicker than Capcom's usual controlled 1-pixel contour.
fixes: Replace the lime pixels with an NES medium blue, using white as the main shell color and black or very dark blue for the outline.
Inset the top and bottom corner pixels by one pixel while widening the middle row to create a clear barrel silhouette.
Reduce the middle band to a cleaner 3-pixel-high strip and preserve a 1-pixel outline around it.
Build each eye as a rounded 3x3 white cluster with clipped corner pixels and a single 1-pixel dark pupil.
Simplify the top and bottom interiors into larger white and blue clusters instead of repeated vertical striping.
Trim one pixel from each heavy lower-corner black cluster and add a single top-left white highlight to give the shell Capcom-style volume.

issues: The side panels are bright chartreuse rather than the described Mega Man-style blue or cyan.
The eyes read as square white windows with square pupils, not two big round robotic eyes.
The full-width black middle band is visually heavy and divides the body into three rigid strips at 1x.
The perfectly mirrored panels and uniform barrel silhouette feel icon-like and static rather than like a Capcom mechanical character.
There is no small underside, nozzle, or other mechanical cue suggesting that the barrel is a floating drone.
fixes: Replace the chartreuse with one NES blue or cyan while retaining black, white, and transparency.
Rebuild each eye as a clipped-corner 3x3 or 4x4 white cluster and offset each 1px pupil toward Mega Man.
Reduce the eye band to a 1px black separator around the eyes instead of a dominant solid stripe.
Narrow the top and bottom by one pixel at each corner to create cleaner stepped barrel curvature.
Convert one or two bottom-edge pixels into a tiny central hover nozzle or paired vents without adding another colour.
Break the strict symmetry with a one-pixel panel, seam, or highlight adjustment in the Capcom style.

issues: The crown and base use bright lime-green vertical bars instead of the described blue, making the drone resemble a striped capsule.
White, lime, black, and a separate near-black navy appear together within the 8x8 regions, exceeding normal NES sprite-palette discipline.
The eyes are blunt square blocks rather than large round mechanical eyes with carefully clipped corners.
The alternating vertical stripes create a modern icon-like pattern instead of Capcom's usual single-shadow, single-highlight volume treatment.
The lower corner steps read as small feet or tabs, weakening the floating barrel silhouette.
At 1x the face reads, but the dark middle band merges heavily with the contour and flattens the body.
fixes: Replace all lime pixels with a medium NES blue and use only transparent, near-black, white, and that blue per sprite palette.
Use one dark outline color consistently; remove the second nearly identical black/navy tone.
Clip one pixel from each eye corner to suggest roundness, keeping compact one-pixel pupils centered or slightly inward.
Replace the repeated top and bottom stripes with one blue shadow column and one small white highlight cluster.
Make the left and right barrel contours symmetrical and remove the bottom corner tabs so the body forms a clean stepped oval.
Thin or interrupt the central dark band near the outer edges so the eyes remain framed without merging into the silhouette.

issues: The body is lime green rather than the specified blue-and-white.
The occupied silhouette is taller than it is wide, so it reads more like a capsule than a squat barrel.
The eye whites and pupils are rigid squares rather than large round mechanical eyes.
The perfectly mirrored top and bottom bands feel generic and lack the small asymmetries typical of Mega Man 2-3 enemy designs.
The thick black middle band visually separates the eyes from the body instead of integrating them into a barrel-like shell.
The clean three-colour palette is NES-compatible, but the bright green-and-white combination does not strongly evoke the intended enemy.
fixes: Replace the lime-green pixels with a medium NES blue and reserve white for the shell highlights and eye whites.
Widen the body by 1 pixel on each side through the middle while trimming 1 pixel from the top and bottom to create a squatter barrel silhouette.
Round each eye by removing the four corner pixels of its white block; keep compact 1-2 pixel black pupils.
Reduce the middle black band by one row and let blue shell pixels frame the eyes at the upper and lower edges.
Add a small one-pixel side nub, seam, or lower thruster break to give the silhouette Capcom-style mechanical character without adding another colour.
Keep the current flat palette and avoid dithering, but simplify the repeated top and bottom stripe pattern into larger, more deliberate clusters.
